name: webpack5-resolve-scheme-vs-resolve-hook-node-protocol
hook: node: URL scheme must be intercepted via resolve.scheme hook, not resolve hook
body: In webpack 5, node: URL scheme requests (node:fs, node:http, etc.) go through resolveForScheme BEFORE the resolve hook chain. resolveForScheme.for('node') returns NodeStuffPlugin when target='node', but if it returns undefined, UnhandledSchemeError is thrown before any resolve hook fires. Tapping the resolve hook (even with stage: -100) CANNOT intercept node: scheme requests — resolveForScheme runs first and throws if no handler exists. The correct approach is to tap the resolve.scheme hook (AsyncSeriesWaterfallHook) to register a handler for the 'node' scheme. This is how NodeStuffPlugin itself registers. Also add the offending package (node-fetch) to serverExternalPackages to prevent webpack from tracing it at all.
why: The previous fix used the resolve hook with stage: -100, believing it would intercept node: requests before webpack's scheme resolver. But resolveForScheme runs BEFORE the resolve hook — UnhandledSchemeError is thrown first, and the resolve hook is never reached. The resolve.scheme hook fires during scheme resolution, allowing interception before the error is thrown.
